stem.en: A charge distribution has zero total charge and zero dipole moment, but a nonzero quadrupole moment. How does its electric potential behave far away, compared to a simple point charge?
stem.et: Laengujaotusel on null kogulaeng ja null dipoolmoment, kuid nullist erinev kvadrupoolmoment. Kuidas käitub selle elektripotentsiaal kaugel, võrreldes lihtsa punktlaenguga?

label.en: It falls off faster than a point charge's 1/r potential — as 1/r^3, the quadrupole term's characteristic falloff, since the lower monopole and dipole terms both vanish.
label.et: See kahaneb kiiremini kui punktlaengu 1/r potentsiaal — 1/r^3-na, kvadrupoolliikme iseloomuliku kahanemisena, kuna madalamad monopool- ja dipoolliikmed mõlemad kaovad.

label.en: It behaves identically to a point charge's potential at any distance, since the multipole expansion means shape never matters.
label.et: See käitub täpselt nagu punktlaengu potentsiaal mistahes kaugusel, kuna multipoolarendus tähendab, et kuju pole kunagi oluline.

label.en: It falls off as 1/r^2, the dipole term's rate, since that's always the leading term for any electrically neutral object.
label.et: See kahaneb 1/r^2-na, dipoolliikme kiirusega, kuna see on alati juhtiv liige iga elektriliselt neutraalse objekti jaoks.

label.en: It is exactly zero everywhere outside the distribution, since the object is both uncharged and non-polar.
label.et: See on täpselt null kõikjal väljaspool jaotust, kuna objekt on nii laenguta kui mittepolaarne.
